headline: Approved rezoning of 625 Clark Avenue to multi-family residential; approved parking revisions at a Stevens Street school.
summary: Voted to prepare a zoning change that would remove large data centers from the zoning use table. Accepted applications for a 7Brew drive-thru restaurant at 650 Farmington Avenue and for earth removal on Grassy Road, and set public hearings for them. Continued the hearings on a racquet club at 575 Broad Street to November 9, 2026.
decisions: Approved the minutes of the September 21, 2026 regular meeting, as amended, 4-0.
Accepted Application #2578 for a fast-food restaurant at 650 Farmington Avenue and set a public hearing for November 9, 2026, 4-0.
Accepted Application #2579 for a site plan at 650 Farmington Avenue and 20 Adeline Avenue and set a public hearing for November 9, 2026, 4-0.
Accepted Applications #2580 and #2581 for earth removal on Grassy Road (Lot 215) and set a public hearing for December 14, 2026, 4-0.
Accepted Applications #2582 and #2583 for a sports court at 18 Treble Road and set a public hearing for December 14, 2026, 4-0.
Voted 4-0 to prepare a zoning text amendment removing the 15,001 to 250,000 square foot data center use from the zoning use table.
Approved change of zone from IP-3 to A (multi-family residential) at 625 Clark Avenue, 4-0, effective November 23, 2026.
Continued the public hearings on the racquet club at 575 Broad Street to November 9, 2026, 4-0.
Approved revisions to Application #2486 for future parking and a batting cage at a public school at 532 Stevens Street, 4-0.

Bristol Zoning Commission Regular Meeting of October 19, 2026 
 
 
 
 
– 1 – 
 
BRISTOL ZONING COMMISSION 
MINUTES 
REGULAR MEETING OF MONDAY OCTOBER 19, 2026 
 
   Place:  City Hall 
    111 North Main St. 
    Council Chambers 
    First Floor 
 
ROLL CALL: 
 
MEMBERS NAME PRESENT ABSENT 
    
REGULAR MEMBERS: David White (Chairman) 
 
X 
 Richard Goodwin (Vice Chairman) X  
 Richard Harlow X  
 John LaFreniere (Secretary) X  
 Sara Mangiafico X  
    
ALTERNATE MEMBERS: Peter Caruso  X 
 Jeffrey Hayden 
 
X 
    
STAFF: Robert M. Flanagan, AICP, City Planner X  
 
1. Call to Order 
 
Per the order of Acting Chairman Goodwin, the meeting was called to order at 6:00 P.M. 
 
Acting Chairman Goodwin reminded the Commission the next regular meeting of the Zoning Commission is Monday, 
November 9, 2026 
 
2. Pledge of Allegiance 
 
3. Public Participation 
 
There was no public participation 
 
4. Approval of Minutes 
 
a. Regular Meeting - September 21, 2026 
 
Acting Chairman Goodwin designated regular Commissioners Mangiafico, Harlow, LaFreniere and Goodwin to vote 
on the September 21, 2026, regular minutes. 
 
Acting Chairman Goodwin noted a correction was needed on page 4, paragraph 2, the first name Francis should be Francisco. 
 
MOTION: Move to approve the minutes of the September 21, 2026, regular meeting, as amended. 
 
By: Goodwin Seconded: Mangiafico. 
 
For: Harlow, Mangiafico, LaFreniere and Goodwin. 
Against: None. 
Abstained: None. 
 
5. Receipt of New Applications
Bristol Zoning Commission Regular Meeting of October 19, 2026 
 
 
 
 
– 2 – 
 
a. Application #2578 — Special Permit for a fast-food restaurant (principal use) and a drive-up facility (accessory use) at 
650 Farmington Avenue; Assessor's Map 48, Lot EPT17+1/8; BG (General Business) zone; 7Brew Company, applicant; 
CNC Real Estate Holdings, LLC, owner. 
 
Acting Chairman Goodwin designated regular Commissioners Mangiafico, Harlow, LaFreniere and Goodwin to vote 
on Application #2578. 
 
Attorney James Ziogas, 104 Bellevue Avenue, representing the applicant, explained this was the location at the Carvel site on 
Farmington Ave. with 2 parcels that had a previous approved Special Permit. Attorney Ziogas noted the Commission previously 
approved a Special Permit to park to the rear of a residential house (Lot 48-20.) The attorney said the proposed restaurant would 
be on Lot 18 and some of the parking would be on Lot 20 so a Special Permit was required for the plan. Attorney Ziogas 
mentioned a Site Plan was required for both of the lots. The attorney noted this would be a drive-thru restaurant. Attorney Ziogas 
reviewed the process for order by I-pads.  
 
Mr. Flanagan noted the plan would refresh the property and there would be no expansion of the building. The City Planner said the 
use was allowed by Special Permit and there was an existing Special Permit for the property.  
 
MOTION: Move that Application #2578 be accepted and scheduled for a Public Hearing for the November 9, 2026 Regular 
meeting of the Zoning Commission. 
 
By: Mangiafico Seconded: Harlow. 
 
For: Mangiafico Harlow, LaFreniere and Goodwin. 
Against: None. 
Abstained: None. 
 
The application is scheduled for public hearing. 
 
b. Application # 2579 — Site Plan for a fast-food restaurant (principal use) and a drive-up facility (accessory use) at 650 
Farmington Avenue and minor site improvements at 20 Adeline Avenue; Assessor's Map 48, Lot EPT17+1/8 and Lot 20; 
BG (General Business) zone and R-10 (Single-Family Residential) zone; 7Brew Company, applicant; CNC Real Estate 
Holdings, LLC, owner. 
 
Acting Chairman Goodwin designated regular Commissioners Mangiafico, Harlow, LaFreniere and Goodwin to vote 
on to vote on Application #2579. 
 
Commission inquiries: Attorney James Ziogas, 104 Bellevue Avenue, representing the applicant, verified the plan was for a two-
lane drive-thru window restaurant with 18 vehicle queuing. Attorney Ziogas noted the site had to be looped. The attorney said 
some of these same facilities hire the police to direct traffic when there are special events. Attorney Ziogas pointed out the Rt. 6 
driveway was closed. Attorney Ziogas indicted the driveway would be paved and restriped. The attorney said the parking lot was 
for employees only. The attorney noted the vacant house would not be improved and remain in its existing condition.  
 
The Commission was concerned the traffic may back up onto Adeline Ave. when there are special events.  
 
MOTION: Move that Application #2579 be accepted and scheduled for a Public Hear ing for the November 9, 2026 Regular 
meeting of the Zoning Commission. 
 
By: Mangiafico Seconded: Harlow. 
 
For: Mangiafico Harlow, LaFreniere and Goodwin. 
Against: None. 
Abstained: None. 
 
The application is scheduled for public hearing. 
 
c. Application #2580 — Special Permit for Earth Removal in excess of 400 cubic yards associated with the development of a 
residential dwelling lot at Grassy Rd. (Lot 215); Assessor's Map 20, Lot 215; R-40 (Single-Family Residential) zone; H&T 
Holdings of Bristol, LLC, applicant.
Bristol Zoning Commission Regular Meeting of October 19, 2026 
 
 
 
 
– 3 – 
 
 
d. Application #2581 — Site Plan for Earth Removal in excess of 400 cubic yards associated with the development of a 
residential dwelling lot at Grassy Rd. (Lot 215); Assessor's Map 20, Lot 215; R-40 (Single-Family Residential) zone; H&T 
Holdings of Bristol, LLC, applicant. 
 
Acting Chairman Goodwin explained Applications #2580 and #2581 would be heard concurrently but voted on separately. 
 
Acting Chairman Goodwin designated regular Commissioners Mangiafico, Harlow, LaFreniere and Goodwin to vote  
on Applications #2580 and #2581. 
 
Attorney James Ziogas, 104 Bellevue Avenue, representing the applicants, noted the applications needed public hearings 
scheduled. Attorney Ziogas  
 
MOTION: Move that Applications #2580 and #2581 be accepted and scheduled for a Public Hearing for the December 14, 2026 
Regular meeting of the Zoning Commission.  
 
By: Mangiafico Seconded: Harlow. 
 
For: Mangiafico Harlow, LaFreniere and Goodwin. 
Against: None. 
Abstained: None. 
 
The Applications #2580 and #2581 are scheduled for public hearing. 
 
e. Application # 2582 — Special Permit for a sports court (accessory use) at 18 Treble Road; Assessor's Map 63, Lot 42; R-
25 (Single-Family Residential) zone; Jeremy and Jennifer Fedorchick, applicants/owners. 
 
f. Application # 2583 — Site Plan for a sports court (accessory use) at 18 Treble Road; Assessor's Map 63, Lot 42; R-25 
(Single-Family Residential) zone; Jeremy and Jennifer Fedorchick, applicants/owners. 
 
Acting Chairman Goodwin explained Applications #2582 and #2583 would be heard concurrently but voted on separately. 
 
Acting Chairman Goodwin designated regular Commissioners Mangiafico, Harlow, LaFreniere and Goodwin to vote  
on Applications #2582 and #2583. 
 
The City Planner indicated the applicants have already constructed the sports court on their property. Mr. Flanagan noted a site 
plan was not received yet but the applicants engineer was done with the plan and it was supposed to be brought in soon.  
 
MOTION: Move that Applications #2582 and #2583 be accepted and scheduled for a Public Hearing for the December 14, 2026, 
Regular meeting of the Zoning Commission.  
 
By: Mangiafico Seconded: Harlow. 
 
For: Mangiafico Harlow, LaFreniere and Goodwin. 
Against: None. 
Abstained: None. 
 
By: Mangiafico Seconded: Harlow. 
 
The Applications #2582 and #2583 are scheduled for public hearing. 
 
6. City Council Referral 
 
a. Data Centers 
 
Acting Chairman Goodwin designated regular Commissioners Mangiafico, Harlow, LaFreniere and Goodwin to vote on City Council 
Referral, Data Centers.
Bristol Zoning Commission Regular Meeting of October 19, 2026 
 
 
 
 
– 4 – 
 
Chairman White at the September meeting indicated that this item would be tabled until this regular meeting. Staff noted that the 
City Council requested that the larger data centers (15,001 sq. ft. and above) be eliminated from the Zoning Regulations. The 
request also stated that the smaller data centers (under 15,000 sq. ft.) should be required to have a special permit and there 
should be a separation distance between data centers.   
 
Information previously received from Eversource was that the current power gird in Connecticut and the New England in general, 
cannot provide the electricity needed to support large scale data centers, so eliminating this item makes sense. The City Planner 
suggested the definition remain in the Regulations, but that the use will be eliminated in the table of uses in Section 4.2.  
 
Acting Chairman Goodwin indicated a response was needed to the City Council. The application for the elimination of the larger 
format data centers will be accepted by the Commission at the January 2027 Regular meeting. 
 
MOTION: Make a motion to prepare a Zoning Text Amendment application to remove the Data Center Special Permit use (15,001 
sq. ft. – 250,000 sq. ft) from the principal use summary table listed in Article II, Section 4.2 of the Zoning Regulations. 
 
The Text Amendment application will be received at the January 2027, Regular meeting and then scheduled for a Public Hearing by 
the Commission, once the application is received.  
 
With respect to the Data Center Site Plan uses (15,000 sq. ft or less) currently allowed in the BHC zone, the referral from Council 
suggested additional restrictions such as adding a Special Permit requirement and adding separation distances between Data Centers. 
The Zoning Commission is not considering any further changes to the Regulations at this time. 
 
By: Mangiafico Seconded: Harlow. 
 
For: Mangiafico Harlow, LaFreniere and Goodwin. 
Against: None. 
Abstained: None. 
 
The application would be received at the January 11, 2027, regular meeting. 
 
7. Public Hearings 
 
a. Application #2573 — Change of Zone from IP-3 (Industrial Park) zone to A (Multi Family Residential) zone at 625 Clark 
Avenue; Assessor's Map 66, Lot 264; Chippens Hill Office Park, LLC, owner/applicant. 
 
Acting Chairman Goodwin designated regular Commissioners Mangiafico, Goodwin, Harlow, LaFreniere and White to vote on 
Applications #2573. 
 
Attorney James Ziogas, 104 Bellevue Avenue, representing the applicant, reviewed the request for change of zone from IP-3 Zone 
to A-Zone for 3.2-acre site located at 625 Clark Avenue. Attorney Ziogas reviewed the previous zone change application that was 
heard by the Commission in March 2026.  This was an extension of a like zone across the street on Clark Avenue. The attorney 
noted the property prior use of was business and medical offices.  
 
Attorney Ziogas stated that during the last application there were 2 doctors’ offices in the building that relocated to Riverside 
Avenue, so the building is now vacant. The attorney said the purpose of the application was to convert the existing building to 
condominiums and to potentially construct a new condominium building to the rear of the site that required a Special Permit and 
Site Plan. Attorney Ziogas noted the property has City sewer and water services. If approved, the attorney’s view was the area 
streets could handle the amount of traffic that would be in the area if approved.  
 
Attorney Ziogas felt the residential reuse would be a good for the building because the building would be vacant for a long time if 
this zone change did not occur. The attorney stated the buildings would be consistent with the POCD and would create new 
housing for Bristol. Attorney Ziogas indicated the plan met the Regulations.  
 
No one else spoke in favor of the application. 
No one spoke against the application. 
 
The following person was not in favor or against the application but had questions: Sherry Duquette, 2014 Matthews St., inquired 
of the total number of units to be constructed and the number of units per building. Ms. Duquette wanted to know if there would 
be any basements in the buildings.
Bristol Zoning Commission Regular Meeting of October 19, 2026 
 
 
 
 
– 5 – 
 
 
The attorney explained there were 2 existing buildings and potentially up to 2 buildings constructed to the rear of the property that 
required Site Plan approval. Attorney Ziogas stated there would be no basements in the buildings but the ground water had to be 
reviewed. The attorney mentioned there may be inland wetlands on adjacent property that had to be reviewed. Attorney Ziogas 
noted there may be 8 units per unit so a total of 24 units but was unsure of the final number of units with the parking and 
setbacks. 
 
Acting Chairman reminded the public audience the application this evening was only for a zone change and the buildings required 
applications.  
 
The following person spoke again: Sherry Duquette inquired if the ingress and egress would remain the same for the site. 
Attorney Ziogas said the accesses would remain the same for the property onto Clark Avenue.  
 
The City Planner review the documents for the application. 
 
The hearing is closed. 
 
By: Mangiafico Seconded: Harlow. 
 
For: Mangiafico Harlow, LaFreniere and Goodwin. 
Against: None. 
Abstained: None. 
 
The Commission thought the plans would fit with the neighborhood. 
 
MOTION: Move that Application #2573 — Change of Zone from IP-3 (Industrial Park) zone to A (Multi- Family Residential) 
zone at 625 Clark Avenue; Assessor's Map 66, Lot 264; Chippens Hill Office Park, LLC, owner/applicant be 
approved. 
 
The Zoning Map amendment, as presented, would be consistent with the goals, policies and action steps of the 2015 Plan of 
Conservation and Development, amended to April 1, 2018. 
 
The effective date of the Zoning Map Amendment shall be: November 23, 2026. 
 
By: Mangiafico Seconded: Harlow. 
 
For: Mangiafico Harlow, LaFreniere and Goodwin. 
Against: None. 
Abstained: None. 
 
The application is approved. 
 
b. Application #2575 — Special Permit for a tennis or racquet club facility at 575 Broad Street; Assessor's Map 39, Lot 72; I 
(General Industrial) zone and BG (General Business) zone; Padel Connect CT, LLC, applicant; Bristol NYCEB, LLC, owner. 
 
c. Application #2576 — Site Plan for a tennis or racquet club facility at 575 Broad Street; Assessor's Map 39, Lot 72; I 
(General Industrial) zone and BG (General Business) zone; Padel Connect CT, LLC, applicant; Bristol NYCEB, LLC, owner. 
 
Acting Chairman Goodwin explained Applications #2575 and #2576 would be heard concurrently but voted on separately. 
 
Acting Chairman Goodwin designated regular Commissioners Mangiafico, Harlow, LaFreniere and Goodwin to vote  
on Applications #2575 and #2576. 
 
Attorney James Ziogas, 104 Bellevue Avenue, representing the applicant, noted this was an industrial building in the former Bristol 
Brass building. Attorney Ziogas indicated the request would only be in a small portion of the building. The attorney said the ingress 
would be on Broad St. Attorney Ziogas verified the applicant received an approval from the Zoning Board of Appeals to reduce the 
parking to 110 parking spaces.
Bristol Zoning Commission Regular Meeting of October 19, 2026 
 
 
 
 
– 6 – 
 
Jagdeep Rughoo, 31 Quail Hollow Dr., Southington, reviewed the process of the sport with the Commission that was popular in 
Europe and South Africa. Mr. Rughoo explained the sport may be played by all ages. The applicant said there would be coaching, 
leagues and teams.  
Mr. Rughoo specified there was an area for a restaurant and there would be socialization after the games. The applicant was 
anticipating there were would be many customers from surrounding towns.  
 
Mr. Flanagan inquiries: Mr. Rughoo verified the peak hours would be from 2:00 P.M. to 4:00 P.M. and at 8:00 P.M. The applicant 
added the facility would not be open every day until the business grows then off-peak hours would be from 9:00 A.M. to 3:00 P.M. 
 
Commission inquiries: The applicant verified the sport was more vigorous than pickle ball but not difficult. Mr. Rughoo specified 
there were two existing facilities in Branford and Norwalk. The applicant noted each game is about 15 minutes similar to tennis. 
 
The attorney pointed out the concerns from last month and that the building exterior including the parking had to be cleaned up 
and restriped. Attorney Ziogas described how the interior of the building would be improved because it was a reuse of an existing 
building. The attorney said the lighting plan for the property would be addressed with the site plan comments. Attorney Ziogas 
noted the applicant was in attendance to review the concerns. 
 
Charles Nyberg, A.I.A., consultant, 225 North Main St., representing the applicant, reviewed the comments. Mr. Nyberg noted 
there was insufficient time to place the comments on the site plans so he reviewed the response comments that would be placed 
on the plans. The consultant stated a photometric plan would be provided for the application. Mr. Nyberg added signage would be 
added to the site for directions and location. The consultant indicated 5 handicapped parking spaces would be added to the plans.  
 
Mr. Nyberg said the hours of business would be from 8:00 A.M. to 10:00 P.M. and there would be 4 employees. The consultant 
noted an environmental review would be conducted for the Bristol-Burlington Health District. Mr. Nyberg indicated the entrances 
would be to the east of the property. The consultant reviewed the 24 ft. aisle width and a tunnel on the west end of the site that 
allows vehicles to drive to the rear of the building from Broad St. Mr. Nyberg noted Liberty Recycling has a service area on the 
site.  
 
Mr. Flanagan had a concern with the unregistered vehicles on the property and the Commission approving the plans. The City 
Planner wanted the unregistered vehicles removed from the property if the plans are approved by the Commission.  
 
City Planner inquiries: Attorney Ziogas mentioned the unregister vehicles were not part of the applicant’s parking area but were on 
the property and the violation needed to be resolved. 
 
The consultant said when Liberty Recycling is able to relocate their items from the site, this area would be cleaned up. Mr. Nyberg 
stated there is only one area for the monument signage and a possible curb cut were not in an ideal area. The consultant thought 
the monument signage should be placed on the east side of the site. Mr. Nyberg reviewed the interior and exterior layout of the 
building. The consultant briefly reviewed the comments and response comments. Mr. Nyberg noted the building is being improved 
and is being nominated for Historic National Registry.  
 
The attorney confirmed that a revised Site Plan is needed for the plans to address the response comments. Attorney Ziogas agreed 
the applications should be continued to the November meeting to resolve all the comments. The attorney indicated the business 
should be able to open in March or April 2027. 
 
No one else spoke in favor of the application. 
No one spoke against the application. 
 
MOTION: Move to continue the Public Hearings on Applications #2575 and #2576 to the November 9, 2026 Regular Meeting of 
the Commission. 
 
By: Mangiafico Seconded: Harlow. 
 
For: Mangiafico Harlow, LaFreniere and Goodwin. 
Against: None. 
Abstained: None. 
 
The Applications #2575 and #2576 are continued.
Bristol Zoning Commission Regular Meeting of October 19, 2026 
 
 
 
 
– 7 – 
 
8. Old Business 
 
There was no old business. 
 
9. New Business 
 
MOTION: Move that Motion to Add to the Item to Agenda Under New Business: 
 
 Application #2486 – Discussion on future parking for Site Plan for a public school at 532 Stevens Street; 
Assessor’s Map 50, Lot A+A1; R-15 (Single-Family Residential) zone; City of Bristol Board of Education, 
applicant. 
 
By: Mangiafico Seconded: Harlow. 
 
For: Mangiafico Harlow, LaFreniere and Goodwin. 
Against: None. 
Abstained: None. 
 
Mr. Flanagan reviewed his previous conversations with Ms. Levesque regarding adding parking/paving before inclement weather 
starts. The City Planner felt it was a good idea for Ms. Levesque to speak to the Commission about this request.  
 
Nancy Levesque, P.E., of Benesch, 200 Glastonbury Blvd., Glastonbury, representing the applicants, explained the new Northeast 
Middle School was being constructed and the old Northeast Middle School was demolished. Ms. Levesque said the contractors are 
working on the parking and athletic areas. The engineer stated the initial plan had 65 future parking spaces and additional 10 
future parking spaces were removed from the plans.  
 
Ms. Levesque verified the applicant received approval for a shed permit for the maintenance staff. The engineer said the applicant 
wanted to construct the 61-space parking lot for large events now versus construct the parking lot in 2 years. Ms. Levesque 
indicated this would keep the plan more cost effective rather than construct in 2 years and be less disruptive for the area.  
 
Staff indicated the previous plan showed 65 future parking spaces opposed to this plan with 61 parking spaces.  
 
The Commission understood with the larger events now that the additional parking would be helpful for the events on premise. 
 
Mr. Flanagan inquiries: The engineer stated the trees were not planted yet since it was in Phase II but the lighting plan was 
installed behind the parking lot on the property. Ms. Levesque indicated one tree may have to be relocated. The engineer indicated 
the paving and parking spaces should be constructed before Thanksgiving. Ms. Levesque noted Phase II has a lot of work 
remaining. 
 
MOTION: Move to approve the revisions to Application #2486 as presented by Nancy Levesque, P.E. for future parking and 
batting cage. 
 
By: Mangiafico Seconded: Harlow. 
 
For: Mangiafico Harlow, LaFreniere and Goodwin. 
Against: None. 
Abstained: None. 
 
The application is approved. 
 
10. Staff Reports 
 
Staff will inform Mr. Brown that the staff report listed 2024 on the report.  
 
11. Adjournment 
 
Acting Chairman Goodwin designated regular Commissioners Mangiafico, Harlow, LaFreniere and Goodwin to vote on the 
adjournment.
Bristol Zoning Commission Regular Meeting of October 19, 2026 
 
 
 
 
– 8 – 
 
 
MOTION: Move to adjourn at 7:15 P.M. 
 
By: Mangiafico Seconded: Harlow. 
 
For: Mangiafico Harlow, LaFreniere and Goodwin. 
Against: None. 
Abstained: None. 
 
This meeting was recorded. 
 
Respectfully submitted, 
 
Nancy King 
Recording Secretary 
 
 
 
David White, Chairman  Richard Goodwin, Secretary
